extracted.intended_audience: Media professionals, entrants/submitters to the Peabody Awards, and the interested public
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the Peabody Awards' selection and adjudication process for annual nominees and winners, including board composition, procedural safeguards, and category handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous deliberative process and face-to-face discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of the annual nominees and winners is based on a rigorous deliberative process and face-to-face discussions among a diverse Board of Jurors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This framing establishes that decisions are reached through deliberation and in-person discussion rather than purely remote or automated means; it is cited as part of the organization's commitment to the integrity of the Awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse Board of Jurors representing varied backgrounds
rubrics_metrics.description: From media professionals and scholars to critics and journalists, the Peabody Board of Jurors is comprised of top-level thought leaders from varied backgrounds to ensure that the annual nominees and winners reflect a broad cross-section of voices, experiences, and audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes diversity of professional perspectives and audiences as a substantive criterion for fair and representative selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Juror appointment, term, and independence safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Each member is appointed by the executive director for a renewable three-year term of service. Board members do not receive payments and all sessions are protected from industry lobbying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies appointment process, term length, non-compensation, and anti-lobbying protections to preserve impartiality and integrity of deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication workflow: initial screening and intensive board meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjudication of more than 1300 entries received annually begins with an initial screening round, leading to three intensive board meetings at which programs are viewed and discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlines the multi-stage review: initial screening to narrow entries followed by three concentrated meetings where submissions are viewed and debated, indicating substantial review effort per entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominee and winner totals per year
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board recognizes 60 nominees, and ultimately, 30 winners each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides overall targets for recognition and awards (60 nominees → 30 winners) as an expectation of scale relative to the annual entry pool (~1300+).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Peabody Awards are given in the categories of entertainment, documentary, news, podcast/radio, arts, children’s and youth, public service, and multimedia programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the topical/format categories under which entries are considered; entrants should submit under the relevant category.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fixed nominee/winner quotas per category
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no set number of nominees or winners in the categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates flexibility in how nominees and winners are distributed across categories—selection is based on merit as determined by the Board rather than category quotas.
